object_description: two compact building volumes linked by a basement
design_condition: The compact wings occupy opposite sides of the elongated plot, forming a nearly square street-facing open space and a tree-lined courtyard with a rear connection, while the sports wing responds to the adjacent park edge and matches the school wing's height.

positive.statement: The urban development setting combines an interesting addition and natural connection of public urban spaces with the school's high usage requirements.
The urban development strategy is reflected in the clever continuation of use units, allowing the school and the city to form a spatial composition.
The space between the two buildings provides a generous access situation and clear addressing of the entrances.
The tree-lined courtyard and the shared areas provide useful common spaces for school operations.
The ground floor can be used very flexibly and efficiently through the overlap of multipurpose use and the entrance hall.
The efficient floor plan concept and the clear arrangement of the outside space are convincing from an operational point of view.
The two buildings impress with good construction values, compactness, resource-saving durability, and a sensible ventilation concept.
The different support structures are reflected in a finely graduated architectural expression of the facades.
The vertically consistent static concept of the compact building parts is economical.

negative.statement: The reduced access and compact floor formation are restrictive on the upper floors because the central zones are occupied.
The classrooms positioned across the façade are unfavorable in their organization and lighting.
The strong building grid limits the flexibility of use.
The internal spaciousness on the upper floors is weakened by the central usage arrangements and loses quality.
The typological approach of separate access areas with a shared center of use contradicts the horizontal flexibility requirements of a vocational school.
The two narrow connecting corridors are poorly usable, leaving the solution indecisive on the upper floors.
The mentioned pile foundation is cost-intensive.
